could a different prior be substantially more robust to score errors?

leak_passages: Tilting the final data distribution directly may be hard to learn, because the score function near the data distribution can be very complicated, whereas the distribution at high noise levels is close to a simple Gaussian; on the other hand, a reward is only defined on the final output, and an intermediate state is only partially informative about the eventual reward. How should one trade off these competing effects, and can shaping the distribution at an intermediate noise level lead to more effective fine-tuning than shaping the final distribution?

These questions matter across domains where diffusion models are used, including text-to-image generation, where generated images should better align with prompts, as well as structured discrete-continuous generation tasks such as layout and molecule generation

avis.comment: Answers are sound. The statement stays at the level of challenges and prior work; it mentions the weak-return ambiguity and optimization against real measurements, which hint at the method but are framed as problem characteristics, so not judged a leak. Classification mostly_experiments / real_only is correct (appendix derivations, all experiments on real collected radar data). Targets are grounded with exact quotes and observable. Compute of 960 H100-hours is an estimate from 32 h per run times about 30 runs; plausible though possibly high if ablations were shorter or shared runs.

targets.comment: Exact quote; matched-filter imaging plus thresholding and Poisson surface reconstruction is the conventional, method-agnostic baseline.
Exact quote; independent camera/LiDAR ground truth with F1 and Chamfer distance is a generic evaluation control (metrics are in the appendix and results).
Exact quote; real data, several objects, line-of-sight and occluded conditions reported separately.
Exact quote; viewpoint/aperture coverage ablation is about the data, not a component of the paper's method.
Exact quote; held-out-view prediction is a reasonable generic check of the fitted forward model, though less essential than C1-C3.
Exact quote from the Overview; end-to-end optimization of an implicit surface through a differentiable RF forward model is the core approach.
Exact quote; sharing density/transmittance across antennas and caching signal tracing (memory bank) are described in the same section; checkable in a plan.
Exact quote from the masking ablation; handling the ambiguity of weak returns is a key finding.
Exact quote; the paper states brute-force per-antenna tracing makes backpropagation infeasible and that training without lensless sampling is infeasible.
Exact quote; plain L2 without masking is shown to give incorrect reconstructions. Mirror image of F3, somewhat redundant.
Exact quote; beamforming in near field is argued and illustrated (appendix wrench heatmap) to distort images; support is more argument than measured comparison.
